b: Month is a time dimension in Amazon Ads unified reporting. Added to a report, it groups every row by calendar month, so impressions, clicks, spend, purchases and sales are summed across the days of January, February and so on rather than shown day by day. It exists because most advertising money is planned, invoiced and judged in months. Budgets are set monthly, agency fees are billed monthly and board packs compare one month with the last. A report at daily grain answers operational questions; a report at monthly grain answers the ones finance asks. Month is also the grain at which Amazon keeps the longest history: up to six years, against 15 months for daily data.
Where Month sits in the unified report

Amazon's unified reporting dimensions page, updated on November 11, 2026, lists 156 attributes in 11 categories. One of them is Time, which holds eight fields: Date, Week, Day of month, Month, Year, Day of week, Hour and Date range. PPC Land's count of that page found that all eight time attributes apply to DVA+, Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display. That makes the Time category one of the few that every major ad product shares, unlike geography or deal fields, which return null for sponsored ads rows. DVA+ is the AI-led display, video and audio campaign type that Amazon introduced on September 29, 2026, when Amazon DSP (demand-side platform) was renamed DVA.

The same page carries a caveat for Sponsored TV: "We do not support Streaming TV Smart mode/ Sponsored TV yet." As of November 2026, monthly figures for Sponsored TV may therefore not appear in a unified report even where the Time fields are marked for it.

Month is rarely read alone. It is usually paired with Year, so that March 2026 and March 2025 do not merge into one row, and sits above Week, Date and Day of month in the hierarchy of time grains. Date range is a different kind of field: it states the reporting window itself and replaces the older "Start Date/ End Date" (sponsored ads) and "Interval start date/ Interval end date" (DSP) names, according to Amazon's reference as reported by PPC Land. Amazon's reference, in the sources reviewed for this article, does not publish the display format of the Month value.
How a monthly row is built

A monthly row is an aggregate, not a separate measurement. Amazon records delivery and conversion events with timestamps, assigns each to a calendar day, and sums the days into months when the Month dimension is selected. Three rules decide which month an event lands in.

The first is the time zone. Amazon does not state a reporting time zone on the unified reporting pages reviewed here. Third-party documentation fills the gap. The Airbyte connector documentation says "all the reports are generated relative to the target profile's timezone," a profile being one advertiser account in one marketplace. AdLabs, a dayparting vendor, says Amazon stores data in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) and converts it to the marketplace's local zone for the console and reports: Pacific time for Amazon.com, Amazon.ca and Amazon.com.mx, London time for Amazon.co.uk, Central European time for Germany, France, Spain, Italy and the Netherlands, and Japan Standard Time for Amazon.co.jp. Under that rule, a purchase at 11:30pm on October 31 in Los Angeles is an October event in a US report, even though it occurred on November 1 in UTC. Microsoft's Xandr platform, by contrast, defaults to US Eastern time but lets users pick any zone per report, according to Microsoft Learn.

The second is attribution. Unified reporting credits attributed conversions to the date of the ad interaction, which Amazon describes as conversion-to-traffic-based reporting. A shopper who clicks a Sponsored Products ad on January 30 and buys on February 8, within a 14-day window, adds a sale to January, not February. A January report pulled on February 1 therefore understates January.

The third is the grain limit. Amazon's November 2025 beta notice set retention by grain: "two weeks for hourly reporting, 15 months for daily or weekly reporting" and "up to six years for monthly, yearly, or summary-grain reporting". A report that asks for 2021 by day returns nothing; the same period by month does.

Calendar months as a reporting unit are as old as accounting, but Amazon's ad tools reached them unevenly. The sponsored ads Reporting API version 3 offered two time units, SUMMARY and DAILY, according to Airbyte's connector documentation, so a monthly view meant pulling daily rows and summing them outside Amazon. Retention was short: Airbyte describes legacy report data as kept for 60 days.

The programmatic side moved first inside the console. On October 6, 2022, Amazon added a Time breakdown to Amazon DSP campaign management tables, letting self-service buyers nest rows under orders and line items and "select one of the time unit grains (daily, weekly. monthly and day of week)", according to Amazon's launch notice. It covered 17 marketplaces.

Unified reporting brought monthly grain to every product in one schema. Amazon opened the beta at its unBoxed conference on November 11, 2025, combining sponsored ads and DSP data in one report builder, with the six-year monthly window. The same day Amazon extended the Amazon Marketing Cloud lookback from 13 to 25 months, a separate clean-room change that also allowed two full years of month-on-month comparison. Unified reporting reached general availability on June 8, 2026, PPC Land reported, when Amazon also set the sunset of legacy Sponsored Ads and Amazon DSP reports. The November 11, 2026 dimensions update then published the Time category's eight fields in their current names.

Monthly grain is where reporting meets money. Agencies and brands commonly reconcile spend against purchase orders and invoices on a monthly cycle, so the Month row is usually the one that has to match the paperwork. It is also the only grain at which November 2026 can be set against November 2021, five Black Fridays apart, because daily data expires after 15 months.

The field also feeds other dimensions. Amazon's Long-term sales cohort dimension is defined as "the calendar month in which the cohort's customers had their new-to-brand conversion attributed to the campaign", according to the reference quoted by PPC Land. Cohort analysis on Amazon is therefore built on calendar months by design.

Months are unequal. February has 28 or 29 days; March has 31. A flat daily run rate produces about 11% more spend in March 2026 than in February 2026 for no reason other than the calendar. Some months also hold five weekends, others four. Monthly totals compare poorly without a per-day normalisation.
Recent months are provisional. Because conversions are credited to the interaction date, the latest month and often the one before it keep changing. Reports pulled on different days disagree.

Time zones split comparisons. If profiles are reported in their own marketplace time zones, a global report combining US and German accounts draws month boundaries nine hours apart. Amazon's own unified reporting pages reviewed here do not state the rule; the evidence comes from third-party connectors and vendors.

Definitions change mid-series. On January 1, 2026, Amazon applied shopping-signal attribution with shorter windows to view-tracked Sponsored Brands, vCPM Sponsored Display and some DSP campaigns, PPC Land reported, splitting ROAS reporting into two metric families. From January 1, 2027, DVA display ads on the Amazon Store will count an impression only once on screen, and Amazon expects 63% fewer impressions on average. Both changes fall on a month boundary, so December-to-January comparisons in 2025-26 and 2026-27 measure methodology as much as performance.

Retail calendars disagree with civil ones. Many retailers report on the National Retail Federation's 4-5-4 calendar, which divides the year into months "based on a 4 weeks - 5 weeks - 4 weeks format" so that "like days are compared to like days," according to NRF. A 53rd week is added roughly every five to six years, most recently in 2023. Amazon's Month is a calendar month, so brand finance teams on a 4-5-4 year must remap it.
Month vs Day of month. Month groups days into a month. Day of month labels each row with its position, from 1 to 31, and is used to spot patterns such as spend spikes after payday.
Month vs Date range. Month is a grouping inside the report. Date range defines the report's start and end. A date range from January 15 to March 15 produces two partial months and one full one.

Calendar month vs retail or broadcast month. Amazon's Month follows the civil calendar. NRF's 4-5-4 months are fixed blocks of four or five weeks, and the standard broadcast calendar used in US television ends each month on its last Sunday. A March total in each system covers different days.
Month vs Long-term sales cohort. Month says when an event was credited. Long-term sales cohort says in which month the customer was first acquired as new to brand, and follows that group forward.

Amazon updated its dimensions reference on November 11, 2026, the page behind PPC Land's 156-field count. On November 12, Amazon published a revised shutdown timeline: legacy reports become read-only on December 17, 2026 and unmigrated reports and their history are deleted on January 31, 2027, a month later than the December 31 date first set. For advertisers with monthly dashboards built on legacy DSP or sponsored ads reports, that means rebuilding them on the unified schema's Month and Year fields before January ends. The first full month in the new schema, January 2027, will also be the first under on-screen impression counting for Amazon Store display.

Who: Amazon Ads defines and reports the Month dimension; advertisers, agencies, finance teams and data engineers use it to reconcile spend and track trends across DVA+, Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display.
What: Month is a Time category dimension that groups unified report rows by calendar month, usually paired with Year, with conversions credited to the month of the ad interaction.

When: Monthly breakdowns reached Amazon DSP tables on October 6, 2022. Unified reporting has offered monthly grain across products since its November 11, 2025 beta, with general availability on June 8, 2026.
Where: In the Time category of Amazon Ads unified reporting, available in the Ads Console, the Reporting API and Amazon Marketing Stream, with up to six years of monthly history.
Why: Budgets, invoices and performance reviews run on months, and monthly grain is the only level at which Amazon keeps more than 15 months of history.
